descriptionChirho: Intransitive/stative sense in the Qal stem (and adjectival form): the subject is, becomes, or will be ritually or morally clean/pure, used of persons, objects, and land after defilement or disease.
Declarative Piel sense where the priest formally pronounces or declares a person or object ritually clean, a technical Levitical term found primarily in the purity laws of Leviticus 13-14.

Causative/factitive Piel sense where the subject actively cleanses, purifies, or makes clean a person, place, or object, used of ritual purification rites, moral cleansing by God, and physical purification of the temple or land.
Reflexive/middle Hitpael sense where the subject purifies himself or herself, or undergoes a process of ritual self-purification, often in preparation for worship or after contact with defilement.
Passive Pual sense indicating that the subject has been cleansed or purified by an external agent, the passive counterpart of the Piel factitive.
